newStack.reason: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, not a regression. The C++ LoopDetector reported ONE face carrying an inner loop; the new stack's planar-cell detector reports both CELLS — the annulus (which owns the hole) and the inner square — because each is independently extrudable and a profile pick must be able to name either. Recorded here so the case keeps the old oracle visible instead of being quietly rewritten to the new answer.
newStack.provenance: src-tauri/tests/wire_contract.rs nested_inner_disk_parity_and_reopen_stability — 'annulus + inner disk' asserts regions.len()==2 with exactly one hole-bearing cell; protocol/SCHEMA.md §7.4 SketchRegions.

arcAndChord.note: faces not empty; exact count not asserted

notes: Region/hole counts feed extrude/revolve profile selection and preview fill (SCHEMA §7.4 SketchRegions -> regions[] with outerLoop + holes[]). The square-with-hole case is the key multi-loop fixture: ONE region, ONE hole => an extrude of it produces a body with a through/blind pocket. The ellipse area is asserted only as '>50' (not an exact value) — recorded as such (approx 56.5 shown for orientation, not as an oracle). Loop detection uses makeRegionDetectionConfig() in the regen path (proto_regeneration Test 1). EXECUTABLE (roadmap C2): each scenario's `sketch.entities` is now the SCHEMA §7.4 entity form of the prose it shipped with, so the corpus runner can drive SketchRegions directly; `sketch.description` keeps the original wording and `sketch.entitiesProvenance` cites the C++ lines the geometry is read from. No expected value moved. The squareWithHole scenario carries a `newStack` block: the region MODEL changed (planar cells, both extrudable) while the hole count did not, and the corpus records both answers rather than replacing the frozen one.
